label: At D1, rises after an unrewarded S1 visit and after consecutive unrewarded trials.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("state", -3) == 1) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 47 sits near -0.95 at D1, +0.98 at GO and -0.97 at D2; timing explains nearly all raw variance. Beyond timing, the variation is almost entirely at D1, where the value is pulled up (toward 0 or positive) by recent lack of reward. It rises after an unrewarded trial that reached S1 (either choice), more after two unrewarded trials in a row, and most after streaks of 3+ unrewarded trials, especially repeated S1-unrewarded visits (the worst-fit windows reach +0.3 after 3-4 S1 failures, often late in the episode). It is lowered after any rewarded trial. GO and D2 barely vary; at D2 there is a small graded rise with belief that S1 is good and when S1 is reached after a1. The free fit adds 3-deep streak indicators (S1-specific and any-state), which the 3-factor short form cannot express; the short form keeps the one-back S1-unrewarded indicator and the two-back unrewarded streak. Observed-only; no future variables used.

issues: The reported scores reproduce: short form test R^2 beyond timing 0.458 (dev 0.460), free fit test 0.553. The additive observed ceiling is 0.54, so the short form reaches about 85% of it.

The S1-specific claim holds. In the profile, D1 residual after unrewarded S1 is +0.128 (a1) and +0.164 (a2), but only +0.025 to +0.029 after unrewarded S2. Swapping the S1 term for a plain prev_reward==0 term drops test R^2 to 0.389.
The 'consecutive unrewarded' claim holds. Dropping the two-back streak term costs about 0.07-0.1 (fitted weight +0.099).

The 'rewarded trial lowers it' term is mostly a re-centring around the fixed timing baseline, not a separate effect. On their own, prev_reward==1 scores 0.147 and prev_reward==0 scores 0.260, and the two are near-complements at D1. Removing it drops test R^2 to 0.363. The label leaving it out is fine, because the label already states the contrast (unrewarded raises the value).

Remaining systematic error: unrewarded streaks of 3 or more are still badly under-predicted. Worst-fit windows have actual values of about +0.1 to +0.4 at D1 against predictions of -0.65 to -0.9, because the short form tops out at a 2-trial streak. This is the gap from 0.458 to 0.553, which the explanation admits; the 3-factor limit blocks any streak count deeper than 2 (tested several accumulator forms and all were rejected).
Misses by phase x previous trial show no other large error class. The biggest cells are D2 after a1 S1 r (+0.04) and D1 after a1 S1 u (-0.025). D2 belief and state effects are about ±0.03.

One variant scores higher but should not be adopted: replacing tv('reward',-2)==0 with tv('reward',-2)!=1 gives test 0.489. That gain only comes from counting the unseen trial before the window start as unrewarded, so it fits a data boundary rather than describing behaviour.
No future or model-output variables are used.
